acceptance: A tracked harness-facts fixture (one record per harness: version, headless command, session flags, permission example, instruction files and size guidance, skill dirs, hooks, autonomous git actions and switches, model families, quota behaviour, evidence with labels) validates against a schema

refresh-profiles renders two regions from the harness-facts fixture, and a hand edit to either is drift. Executor template: for a profile whose family a harness executor_template.renders_cli_for lists, access.cli is that template with {api_id} replaced by the profile's api_id. The only shape this criterion requires is the shipped one: a single-line block-style value indented two spaces (`  cli: <value>`) under a block-style `access:` mapping whose other children are indented two spaces. A missing `  cli:` line under that mapping is inserted at that indentation. --render rewrites that line so the parsed access.cli equals the rendered value and every other byte stays unchanged. README: the model-profiles harness block between the harness-facts markers is rewritten from the fixture. A README with no block is behind, and --check exits 0 for behind. Drift is a parseable profile whose access.cli differs from the rendered value, or marker bytes that differ from the rendered block. --check exits 1 on drift. --render exits 0 only when every file it changes parses and matches. Any other layout (folded or literal scalar, flow mapping, or any other indentation) may be rewritten only when that same parse-and-match result holds; otherwise the file stays byte-identical and --render exits non-zero. A profile whose front matter does not parse is drift. Round-tripping every YAML encoding is out of scope.

A version-bump diff of --version, --help and inventories is classified before a refresh is accepted; a new identifier containing plan, memory, task, todo, worktree, branch, commit, push, pr, background, delegate, cloud, schedule, review, resume, fork or autopilot fails the diff until it is assigned a relationship

acceptance: Claude Code launches pass an explicit permission mode and allowed tools, no permission prompts, and the retry watchdog with a capped usage-limit wait; a worker stopped by a usage limit enters a paused-by-limit state that worker resume picks up after the reset
Codex launches use exec --json with the workspace-write sandbox, both memory switches off and a per-profile CODEX_HOME; Cursor launches create the chat first and pass --force --trust and never -w

After every turn the adapter records one post_run_check, and the worker's exit code does not skip it. A turn is a harness process the runner started, a start that fails with OSError before a process exists, or a record already terminated when the runner finishes the turn. Stream findings are a permission denial, a failed turn (an error event with no later turn_completed), and an api_retry. Git findings are a branch-name change; a HEAD that is missing or not a descendant of the start HEAD; a commit in that descendant range that changes a path outside the leaf's touch zones; a stash-list change; and a porcelain change on a path that is not an expected file. Expected files are this leaf's bookkeeping (work/brief-<id>.md, work/implementation-summary-<id>.md, work/prompt-<id>-*, this leaf's worker logs, work/reviews/, work/.sessions/, work/.workers/, work/.worktrees/) and roadmap/registry.yaml. A porcelain change is a path newly in the dirty set, a path whose worktree bytes or symlink target differ from the start snapshot, or a path that was dirty at the start and is absent from porcelain at the end. A porcelain XY or index change that leaves the dirty-path set and the worktree content unchanged is not a finding, and neither is file mode, skip-worktree, assume-unchanged, or rename pairing beyond the path names porcelain lists. A finding sets post_run_findings, which worker sync shows; a turn with no finding clears that flag. An A1 usage limit may be recorded on the same event; it is not a fourth stream class.

acceptance: The reviewer prompt asks for a final JSON object matching the review-record schema (Claude --json-schema, Codex --output-schema, Antigravity --json-schema; plain final-message JSON elsewhere) and the adapter writes work/reviews/<ID>/REVIEW-<model>.md from it
A reviewer run that writes any file other than its notes is reported as a review failure
A malformed or missing structured output is reported as a rerun request, never recorded as a verdict

The default Claude Code reviewer launch, which runs --bare and so fires no hook, passes --disallowedTools "Bash(git commit *)" "Bash(git push *)" "Bash(gh *)" beside its allowed tools; a test pins the argv.

Cursor reviewer runs drop --force and pass --mode ask --trust, and Codex reviewer runs use sandbox_mode=read-only with the verdict taken from --output-schema / -o, so docs/design-notes/M8.7-runtime-verification-harness-facts.md ('Review-only runs omit --force') matches the code; tests pin both argv.

Executor avoid lists name each feature with the switch the launch applies: Claude auto memory (shared by every worktree of a repository) and background tasks and /loop wakeups; Codex memories, multi_agent and goals (--disable <feature>); Cursor persist, /goal and cloud handoff (no switch: never invoked; denied where a permission token exists); a test pins the Codex argv with the --disable flags.

acceptance: A Copilot CLI reviewer profile (model pinned, deny git push and gh pr, one-shot) and an Antigravity agy generic profile exist, each marked by the runtime checks that passed

The Copilot reviewer profile's command passes -p, -s, --no-ask-user and --deny-tool for shell(git push), shell(git commit) and shell(gh), never --autopilot, --share-gist, --allow-all or --yolo, and is checked against a captured copilot --help of v1.0.105 or later.

The agy profile's command sets --output-format json (or stream-json) and an explicit --print-timeout, and success is read from the envelope's status (SUCCESS), not the exit code, since permission denials and benign tool errors exit 0 from 1.3.4; the version comes from a captured agy --version (the two reports disagree: 1.4.3 vs 1.4.10).
